The plan

Every Royal Counts, in four parts.

01

The grade race

TK through 12th grade compete on the share of families who give. Never on dollars.

02

The 24-hour clock

One live page on December 1. Donors count up, milestones fall, every grade’s progress is on screen.

03

The unlock

A sponsor promises a gift if enough families give by 8 pm. The whole school pushes toward it.

04

Class reps

Two parents per grade do the asking. We hand them everything they need.

A week of meals for neighbors, and Christian education.

854

weeks’ worth of meals for people in need so far · DEMO

“Every $100 provides a week’s worth of meals for people in need through Feeding America Riverside | San Bernardino, and helps Woodcrest provide Christian education.”

Grandparents, alumni and neighbors who would never give to a school’s budget will give to feed a family. The meals counter on the page turns every gift into something everyone can see.

The grade race

Families count. Dollars don’t.

Each grade’s score is the share of its families who give at least once. A $25 gift moves the board as much as $2,500.

Screens show “4th grade: 41% of families,” never names or amounts. Prizes celebrate a whole grade, so no child is singled out.

66%

family participation for the winning class at Delbarton School in a single Giving Tuesday (2024)

The 24-hour clock

December 1 runs on one live page.

336donors so farDEMO · 7:20 PM
  • 24 hours on a dial. Each hour fills as gifts come in.
  • A live donor count with milestones at 100, 200, 350 and 500.
  • Recent gifts by first name and grade, never amounts.
  • Power hours, the white dots, timed to drop-off, lunch, pickup and family night.

Class reps

Parents ask parents. We do the work for them.

7%

of donors share an appeal on their own. Most people give when someone they know asks them directly.

What every class rep gets

  • A personal link that credits their grade
  • Ready-to-send texts for every day of the warm-up
  • A five-minute training and a one-page playbook
  • Live progress, so they know who still needs a nudge
  • A thank-you note to send the moment a family gives
Sources: Castillo, Petrie & Wardell (2014); Meer (2011).10
The team nobody has asked yet

Grandparents and alumni.

27%

of Crean Lutheran’s 2023 Giving Tuesday donors were grandparents

15%

of Timothy Christian’s 2024 donors were grandparents, with their own challenge gift

49

graduating classes since 1978, organized by class year

Every gift asks one question: How are you connected to Woodcrest? Grandparents pick their grandchild’s grade, alumni add their class year, and every answer fills a gap in your records.

Sources: Crean Lutheran and Timothy Christian giving-day pages on GiveCampus.11
Handled with care

Faculty and students are protected by design.

Faculty and staff

  • A confidential, any-amount staff drive before December 1, shared only as a percentage
  • Announced at launch: the people closest to students are already in
  • Teachers never ask the parents of their own students

Students

  • No student fundraising pages
  • Thank-you videos only with media releases on file
  • Grade prizes celebrate the whole grade, never donor families alone

03

Nov 16 to 20

Tue, Dec 1

of first-time donors give again the next year when nobody follows up

The spring day

Royals Return: the Class Year Challenge.

01

Class years race

Every class since 1978 races on the share of classmates who give. A small class can win.

02

Class agents ask

One or two alumni per class text their classmates. We hand them the kit.

03

Classes challenge classes

“Class of ’99 adds $1,000 if 20 classmates give.” Alumni fund the challenges.

04

Give in honor of a teacher

Any gift can name a favorite teacher. Every honored teacher hears about it.

Every dollar stays at Woodcrest. One alumni unlock: if [300] alumni give by midnight, [an alumni family] adds $[25,000].

Royals Return is a working name. Dates, fund, and sponsor amounts in [brackets] are for Woodcrest to set.24
